source.source_identity: arXiv 2610.20492v1, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling
source.selected_scope: S4.SS1 / S4.E11 / the affine matrix-and-reply fragment of S4.Thmtheorem2 (Remark 4.2), with S2 exact-oracle definitions.

independent_source_reconstruction.setup: For each integer d>=2 and each real kappa>=2, index i=1,...,d and set theta_i=((i-1/2)*pi)/d, lambda_i(kappa)=(kappa+1)/2+((kappa-1)/2)*cos(theta_i), Lambda_kappa=diag(lambda_1(kappa),...,lambda_d(kappa)). For the same orthogonal O in O(d), put A_kappa=O Lambda_kappa O^T and A_2=O Lambda_2 O^T. The source samples O from Haar independently of the algorithm seed, but the algebraic identity is pointwise for every such O.
independent_source_reconstruction.forward_vector_reply: For every x in R^d, A_kappa x=(kappa-1)(A_2 x)-(kappa-2)x.
independent_source_reconstruction.reverse_vector_reply: For every x in R^d, A_2 x=(A_kappa x+(kappa-2)x)/(kappa-1). The denominator is nonzero as a consequence of kappa>=2.
independent_source_reconstruction.oracle_definition: FO_A(x)=(f_A(x), A x), where f_A(x)=(1/2) x^T A x; the scalar component is a function value, the vector component is the exact gradient/matrix-vector reply.
independent_source_reconstruction.forward_exact_first_order_reply: If FO_{A_2}(x)=(v,g), the corresponding reply for A_kappa at that same x is ((kappa-1)v-(kappa-2)||x||^2/2, (kappa-1)g-(kappa-2)x).
independent_source_reconstruction.reverse_exact_first_order_reply: If FO_{A_kappa}(x)=(v,g), the corresponding reply for A_2 at that same x is ((v+(kappa-2)||x||^2/2)/(kappa-1), (g+(kappa-2)x)/(kappa-1)).
independent_source_reconstruction.endpoint: At kappa=2, A_kappa=A_2 and both reply transformations are the identity.

expectation: Actual source cosine-grid diagonal matrices Lambda_kappa and Lambda_2, and their precision matrices formed with one and the same orthogonal rotation O.
A query x and its exact vector reply; when value-and-gradient replies are represented, the reply is the ordered scalar-vector pair ((1/2)x^T A x,A x).

The spectrum is deterministic and may be known to the algorithm; its hidden component is the eigenbasis O. The source target N(0,A^{-1}) is associated context, not an object whose law is transported by the reply identity.
Source hard-family range: integer d>=2; real kappa>=2; i=1,...,d; O is a real d by d orthogonal matrix; x is in R^d.
The same grid angles occur at kappa and at 2. If a zero-based finite index is used later, it must represent ((i+1/2)pi)/d; this is only reindexing.
Source Section 2 defines a larger ambient precision class for d>=1 and kappa>=1. Its ambient range does not silently replace the narrower Section 4.1 public hard-family range.
For every admissible d and kappa and every fixed orthogonal O, form both actual matrices with the same O; then for every query x both vector-reply equalities hold.

The source Haar draw is independent of algorithm private randomness. The bounded algebraic conclusion holds pointwise in O and therefore needs no probabilistic event or almost-everywhere qualification.

A same-O construction cannot be replaced by unrelated matrices having only the same eigenvalues; the affine identity is tied to their common eigenbasis. No existential arbitrary A_2 witness should obscure the source-defined kappa=2 matrix.

Use the actual source grid, source d>=2 and kappa>=2, and orthogonality/common rotation. Haar independence belongs to the random-family construction; no random-law premise is needed for the pointwise algebra.
kappa-1 is positive/nonzero internally from kappa>=2; it is not a new independent source hypothesis.

The response is exact. No finite arithmetic precision, noise tolerance, numerical stability requirement, Gaussian concentration event, Krylov bound, target moment estimate, or algorithm-success premise is part of this reply conversion.

Do not add large-d, delta, an upper cap on kappa, or positive-epsilon assumptions from a different lower-bound theorem to this source fragment. The parent assignment explicitly separates those later-theorem conditions; their exact theorem statement has not been audited in phase one.
Exact matrix identity A_kappa=(kappa-1)A_2-(kappa-2)I_d for this family; exact forward and reverse same-query vector-reply conversions.

Using the source exact first-order definition, the scalar reply transforms with the same affine coefficient and the correction (kappa-2)||x||^2/2. The reverse divides the full corrected pair by kappa-1.

These formulas determine the corresponding actual reply at the same x from either matrix, without knowing O. A statement only about an arbitrary assumed affine matrix relation is reusable algebra, but it does not by itself establish the actual source-family instantiation.

This is algebra of precision matrices and exact oracle replies at a fixed x, including pointwise inverse conversion in both directions. Precision here denotes the inverse covariance matrix; it is not a claim about machine precision.

Section 2 separately states equivalence of exact value-and-gradient, gradient-only and matrix-vector access on one quadratic-input class, because Ax determines the value (1/2)<x,Ax>. Preserve this semantic connection when interpreting any first-order reply type.

The cross-matrix reply identity does not alone give equality/transport of Gaussian target laws, total variation error, tolerance, finite-bit precision, expected or worst-case costs, a complete Borel adaptive-algorithm simulation, or the later lower-bound theorem. Such claims require their own statements and proofs.

The rest of Remark 4.2 discusses the cosine separating statistic, n=2q+1, a Krylov bound and target moments. Those are genuine later proof ingredients, excluded from the bounded affine-reply conclusion and never inferred from it.

Forward scale a=kappa-1 and shift b=kappa-2 depend only on kappa. The reverse coefficient is 1/(kappa-1). The correction uses the known query x, and the scalar correction has the source normalization 1/2.
d occurs in the grid angles and matrix/vector dimensions; there is no d-dependent conversion coefficient. O affects the actual replies but is not needed as input to the reply-conversion formulas.

No unnamed universal constants, delta-dependent constants, dimension threshold, epsilon threshold or kappa upper bound occur in this affine conversion claim. No source lower-bound constant is fixed by these identities.

source_only_derivation: At kappa=2, lambda_i(2)=3/2+(1/2)cos(theta_i). Direct expansion gives (kappa-1)lambda_i(2)-(kappa-2)=(kappa+1)/2+((kappa-1)/2)cos(theta_i)=lambda_i(kappa).
The diagonal identity is Lambda_kappa=(kappa-1)Lambda_2-(kappa-2)I_d. Conjugating by the same O and using O O^T=I_d gives the source precision identity.
Apply the matrix identity to x. Rearrangement and kappa-1 nonzero give the reverse vector-reply formula.
Contract each vector identity with x and divide by 2 to obtain the exact potential-value formula. Pair scalar and vector formulas to obtain both exact first-order reply transformations.
The formulas use only kappa, the given x and the returned reply. They do not use the unknown rotation. At kappa=2 all correction terms vanish and all scales are 1.
